instrument: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
location: Article 9(1)-(9) (Chapter III, Section 2) – Risk management system
provision_text: A risk management system shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained in relation to high-risk AI systems.

instrument: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
location: Article 10(1)-(4), (6) (Chapter III, Section 2) – Data and data governance; read with Article 4a(1)
provision_text: Training, validation and testing data sets shall be subject to data governance and management practices appropriate for the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system.

instrument: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
location: Article 13(1)-(3) (Chapter III, Section 2) – Transparency and provision of information to deployers
provision_text: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way as to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret a system’s output and use it appropriately.

instrument: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
location: Article 14(1)-(4) (Chapter III, Section 2) – Human oversight
provision_text: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way, including with appropriate human-machine interface tools, that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use.

instrument: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
location: Article 15(1), (3)-(5) (Chapter III, Section 2) – Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
provision_text: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way that they achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity, and that they perform consistently in those respects throughout their lifecycle.

instrument: India AI Governance Guidelines: Enabling Safe and Trusted AI Innovation (MeitY, IndiaAI Mission, 5 November 2025)
location: Part 4 – Practical Guidelines for Industry & Regulators; 'Guidelines for industry', bullet 5 (transparency reports)
provision_text: Publish transparency reports that evaluate the risk of harm to individuals and society in the Indian context.

instrument: India AI Governance Guidelines: Enabling Safe and Trusted AI Innovation (MeitY, IndiaAI Mission, 5 November 2025)
location: Part 2, §2.5 Accountability – Recommendations, bullet 2 (proportionate obligations across the AI value chain); read with 'Liability' (graded liability)
provision_text: Impose obligations for each of these entities that are proportionate to their function and the risk of harm

instrument: India AI Governance Guidelines: Enabling Safe and Trusted AI Innovation (MeitY, IndiaAI Mission, 5 November 2025)
location: Part 2, §2.4 Risk Mitigation – Recommendations, bullet 1 (India-specific risk assessment and classification framework)
provision_text: Develop a risk assessment and classification framework that is customised for India’s local context, and accounts for risks to vulnerable groups.

instrument: India AI Governance Guidelines: Enabling Safe and Trusted AI Innovation (MeitY, IndiaAI Mission, 5 November 2025)
location: Part 2, §2.6 Institutions – B. AI Safety Institute (functions)
provision_text: It should test and evaluate AI systems for risks and provide advice to policymakers and industry actors on issues of AI safety.

instrument: India AI Governance Guidelines: Enabling Safe and Trusted AI Innovation (MeitY, IndiaAI Mission, 5 November 2025)
location: Part 2, §2.6 Institutions – whole-of-government approach, bullet 1 (sectoral regulators lead on enforcement)
provision_text: The relevant sectoral agencies and regulators should take the lead in monitoring harms, providing guidance and enforcing regulations in their respective domains.

location: Part 3, §3.2.3 A principles-based approach – Principle: Appropriate transparency and explainability
provision_text: AI systems should be appropriately transparent and explainable.

instrument: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation (DSIT White Paper, CP 815, March 2023; amended version)
location: Part 3, §3.2.3 – Principle: Accountability and governance; read with §3.3.2 Government's role in addressing accountability across the life cycle (paras 80-83)
provision_text: Governance measures should be in place to ensure effective oversight of the supply and use of AI systems, with clear lines of accountability established across the AI life cycle.

instrument: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation (DSIT White Paper, CP 815, March 2023; amended version)
location: Part 3, §3.3.1 New central functions to support the framework – Box 3.1 (Functions required to support implementation of the framework): Cross-sectoral risk assessment (Activities, bullet 1)
provision_text: Develop and maintain a cross-economy, society-wide AI risk register to support regulators’ internal risks assessments.

instrument: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation (DSIT White Paper, CP 815, March 2023; amended version)
location: Part 3, §3.2.3 – Principle: Safety, security and robustness
provision_text: AI systems should function in a robust, secure and safe way throughout the AI life cycle, and risks should be continually identified, assessed and managed.

instrument: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation (DSIT White Paper, CP 815, March 2023; amended version)
location: Part 3, §3.2.4 Our preferred model for applying the principles – para 55 (read with paras 56-59)
provision_text: Initially, the principles will be issued by government on a non-statutory basis and applied by regulators within their remits.

instrument: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation: government response to consultation (DSIT, CP 1019, 6 February 2024)
location: Paragraph 15 (Section 5.1); regulators listed in footnote 28
provision_text: The government has written to a number of regulators impacted by AI to ask them to publish an update … It is important that the public have full visibility of how regulators are incorporating the principles into their work.

location: Paragraph 72 (Section 5.2, highly capable general-purpose AI); see also paragraph 60

instrument: Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (adopted 22 May 2019; revised 8 November 2023 and 3 May 2024)
location: Section 1, Principle 1.3 Transparency and explainability (i)-(iv)
provision_text: AI Actors should commit to transparency and responsible disclosure regarding AI systems.

instrument: Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (adopted 22 May 2019; revised 8 November 2023 and 3 May 2024)
location: Section 1, Principle 1.5 Accountability, paragraphs (a)-(b)
provision_text: AI actors should be accountable for the proper functioning of AI systems and for the respect of the above principles, based on their roles, the context, and consistent with the state of the art.

instrument: Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (adopted 22 May 2019; revised 8 November 2023 and 3 May 2024)
location: Section 1, Principle 1.5 Accountability, paragraph (c) (systematic risk management)
provision_text: AI actors, should, based on their roles, the context, and their ability to act, apply a systematic risk management approach to each phase of the AI system lifecycle on an ongoing basis

instrument: Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (adopted 22 May 2019; revised 8 November 2023 and 3 May 2024)
location: Section 1, Principle 1.4 Robustness, security and safety, paragraphs (a)-(c)
provision_text: AI systems should be robust, secure and safe throughout their entire lifecycle so that, in conditions of normal use, foreseeable use or misuse, or other adverse conditions, they function appropriately and do not pose unreasonable safety and/or security risks.

instrument: Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (adopted 22 May 2019; revised 8 November 2023 and 3 May 2024)
location: Section VIII (instructions to the Digital Policy Committee), point (d); read with points (a)-(c)
provision_text: report to Council, in consultation with other relevant committees, on the implementation, dissemination and continued relevance of this Recommendation no later than five years following its revision and at least every ten years thereafter.
